podcast.title: Architectural Influence on Development
podcast.body: The evolution of gothic music is directly linked to the acoustic properties of medieval stone cathedrals. Hildegard von Bingen's slow, somber sacred monophony, designed to be harmonious with the long echoes and reverb of these cavernous spaces, established a style of chanting and composition that adapted to and utilized the architectural technology. This early form twisted and evolved through centuries, leading directly to modern gothic music culture. "The technology of architecture influenced the composition of music, and it was this gothic music that evolved and twisted in shape until we get modern gothic music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Literary and Legendary Inspirations
podcast.body: Gothic bands were described as groups "raised at a diet of Frankenstein novels and vampire legends and tales of the underworld," drawing heavily on dark, macabre, and fantasy themes. "Then there was the wave of groups described as Gothic. Bands that seemed to be raised at a diet of Frankenstein novels and vampire legends and tales of the underworld."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: Many elements that would later form gothic and sinister music were beginning to emerge around 1979, alongside New Wave and Dark Wave. This era was a fertile ground for the birth and ramification of new musical directions. "muchas partes de lo que sería luego la música agótica y siniestra."

podcast.title: Popularity in Years Ahead
podcast.body: The gothic musical approach, exemplified by bands like Bauhaus, proved to be very popular and influential in the years following its emergence. "Bauhaus' Gothic approach would prove to be very popular in the years ahead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
